title: Sell Mineral Rights in Poplar, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Poplar, MT
metaDescription: Poplar, MT sits over the historic Poplar Field, discovered 1952, on a mix of Fort Peck trust and fee land. I buy mineral interests here, both kinds, directly.
heroLead: The town of Poplar sits right over the field that bears its name, one of the oldest producing areas in this part of Montana.
intro: Poplar Field was discovered in 1952, decades before the Bakken boom, and it's been declining slowly ever since — a long, mature tail rather than a hot new play. What makes a Poplar-area interest more complicated than that history alone suggests is land status: this ground sits within the Fort Peck Reservation, and ownership can be trust land administered by the Bureau of Indian Affairs, fee land held privately, or in some cases a mix within the same family. I sort out which situation applies to your interest before anything else.

I've worked enough of these Fort Peck-area interests to know that skipping the land-status question first is how a deal falls apart later. It's the very first thing I check, before I ever pull a production record.

sections.heading: Trust land and what it means for a sale
paragraphs: If your family's interest is held in trust, a sale requires BIA approval, which follows a different timeline and process than a standard county-recorded transaction. I'm upfront about that from the first conversation rather than letting it surface as a surprise partway through.

sections.heading: A field this old means real decline
paragraphs: Poplar Field has been producing for over seventy years. Whatever royalty stream exists today reflects a mature, low-rate field, not boom-era volumes. I look at actual current production tied to your specific interest before I discuss a number.

sections.heading: Confirming the record before I offer anything
paragraphs: For fee land, I pull the recorded chain from the Roosevelt County Clerk and Recorder in Wolf Point. For trust land, I work through the BIA agency records covering the parcel. Either way, I match the legal description against what your family believes it holds before discussing a number.

faqs.question: Is my Poplar-area interest trust land or fee land?
faqs.answer: That depends on your family's specific history with the parcel. I confirm this first, since it changes the entire sale process.

faqs.question: How old is the Poplar Field, really?
faqs.answer: Discovered in 1952. It's a mature, long-declining field today, and I price interests against that reality rather than newer-play expectations.

faqs.question: Does BIA involvement slow down a sale?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the interest is trust land — I explain the added timeline honestly before we start.

faqs.question: What if my family holds both trust and fee interests near Poplar?
faqs.answer: That happens. I evaluate each piece under its own process rather than forcing them into a single transaction.
